prompt: Let $f(x)=15x-2016$. If $f(f(f(f(f(x)))))=f(x)$, find the sum of all possible values of $x$.

For positive real numbers $x$ and $y$, let $f(x,y)=x^{\log_2 y}$. The sum of the solutions to the equation $$4096\,f(f(x,x),x)=x^{13}$$ can be written in simplest form as $\frac{m}{n}$. Compute $m+n$.

Suppose that $P$ is a polynomial with integer coefficients such that $P(1)=2$, $P(2)=3$ and $P(3)=2016$. If $N$ is the smallest possible positive value of $P(2016)$, find the remainder when $N$ is divided by 2016.
Define a sequence $a_i$ as follows: $a_1=181$ and for $i\ge2$, $a_i=a_{i-1}^2-1$ if $a_{i-1}$ is odd and $a_i=a_{i-1}/2$ if $a_{i-1}$ is even. Find the least $i$ such that $a_i=0$.

Let $[a,b]=ab-a-b$. Shaq sees the numbers $2,3,\ldots,101$ written on a blackboard. Let $V$ be the largest number that Shaq can obtain by repeatedly choosing two numbers $a,b$ on the board and replacing them with $[a,b]$ until there is only one number left. Suppose $N$ is the integer with $N!$ nearest to $V$. Find the nearest integer to $10^6\cdot\frac{|V-N!|}{N!}$.

solutions.title: Greedy combining and an exact formula
solutions.body:
Note $[a,b]=(a-1)(b-1)-1$. The largest result comes from always combining the current number with the next largest: $V=[[\cdots[[101,100],99],\cdots],2]$ (the official solution uses this; I also checked it by brute force on the lists $2,\dots,n$ for $n\le7$).

Let $u=x-1$ for the current number $x$. Absorbing $b$ gives $u\mapsto u(b-1)-2$. Starting from $u=100$ and absorbing $b=100,99,\dots,2$ (multipliers $99,98,\dots,1$):
$$u_{\text{final}}=100!-2\left(98!+97!+\cdots+1!+0!\right),\qquad V=u_{\text{final}}+1.$$
So $N=100$ and
$$10^6\frac{|V-N!|}{N!}\approx2\cdot10^6\left(\frac1{100\cdot99}+\frac1{100\cdot99\cdot98}+\cdots\right)\approx2\cdot10^4\left(\frac1{99}+\frac1{99\cdot98}\right)\approx204.1,$$
since the later terms are far below $1$. The nearest integer is $204$ (exact evaluation gives $204.103\ldots$).

**Answer: 204**

prompt: Let $S_P$ be the set of all polynomials $P$ with complex coefficients, such that $P(x^2)=P(x)P(x-1)$ for all complex numbers $x$. Suppose $P_0$ is the polynomial in $S_P$ of maximal degree such that $P_0(1)\mid2016$. Find $P_0(10)$.

Define the function $f:\mathbb R\setminus\{-1,1\}\to\mathbb R$ to be $$f(x)=\sum_{a,b=0}^{\infty}\frac{x^{2^a3^b}}{1-x^{2^{a+1}3^{b+1}}}.$$ Suppose that $f(y)-f\!\left(\frac1y\right)=2016$. Then $y$ can be written in simplest form as $\frac pq$. Find $p+q$.

solutions.title: Telescope into a geometric series
solutions.body:
Write $m=2^a3^b$. For $|x|<1$,
$$f(1/x)=\sum\frac{x^{-m}}{1-x^{-6m}}=-\sum\frac{x^{5m}}{1-x^{6m}},\quad\text{so}\quad f(x)-f(1/x)=\sum_{a,b\ge0}\frac{x^m+x^{5m}}{1-x^{6m}}.$$
Now $\frac{x^m+x^{5m}}{1-x^{6m}}=\sum_{u\ge0}\left(x^{m(6u+1)}+x^{m(6u+5)}\right)$ is the sum of $x^{mk}$ over all $k\ge1$ coprime to $6$. Every positive integer $v$ is written uniquely as $2^a3^bk$ with $\gcd(k,6)=1$, so each power $x^v$ appears exactly once:
$$f(x)-f(1/x)=\sum_{v\ge1}x^v=\frac{x}{1-x}\quad(|x|<1).$$
For $|x|>1$ the same identity applied to $1/x$ gives $f(x)-f(1/x)=-\frac{1/x}{1-1/x}=\frac1{1-x}$, whose values on $|x|>1$ lie in $(-\infty,0)\cup(0,\tfrac12)$, so $2016$ is impossible there. Hence $|y|<1$ and $\frac{y}{1-y}=2016$, giving $y=\frac{2016}{2017}$ and $p+q=4033$.

**Answer: 4033**
